steps: Remove the door & set the unit

Release the two spring latches and lift the glass door frame off its bottom track. Place the unit to the Figure 3 and 4 clearances, away from traffic, furniture and draperies, and fit the loose top standoffs once it's in position.

Install and vent to CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or the National Fuel Gas Code, ANSI Z223.1 (USA), and local codes. In Massachusetts only a licensed plumber and gas fitter may install it. In a manufactured home (where approved, after the "first sale") the fireplace must be fastened in place.

Door frame removal (unit off and cool)

  1. Pry the top of the safety barrier screen toward you and lift it off its tabs at the base of the door frame; remove the trim kit if installed.
  2. Push a screwdriver against the notch in the top of each latch, grab the latch handle as it protrudes and lift until the hook disengages. Support the door so it doesn't tip out.
  3. Tilt the top of the frame out, then lift it up and out of its bottom track. Store it safely: the ceramic glass is very fragile.

On reassembly the latch handle should snap in flush with the door frame; pulled at the top corners under moderate pressure, the door should come forward and return evenly on both sides.

Locate the unit out of high-traffic areas and away from furniture and draperies, keeping the clearances in Figures 3 and 4. The top standoffs ship loose inside the fireplace: install them on top once it's in position.
Steel stud framing kit

Assemble the supplied kit (TC36.B2FRKITA regular, TC36.BRFRKITA arched), fasten it to the unit's framing brackets with the screw-hole side toward the fireplace, then secure it to the existing framing.

The fireplace should be in place and venting installed before framing in. The supplied steel stud framing kit must be used unless the fireplace is totally enclosed with non-combustible material, such as facing brick.

  1. Lay out the inner and outer vertical side studs and the vertical center studs; screw the upper header stud and the stud plate to the center studs.
  2. Attach the inner and outer side studs to the header stud and fasten them at the bottom with the base plates.
  3. Arch: attach the diagonal arch support studs to the lower horizontal studs and the inner vertical studs.
  4. Align the frame with the unit's framing brackets and fasten through the access holes in the outer side studs, screw-hole side facing the fireplace.
  5. Secure the frame to the existing framing through the upper horizontal stud and the stud plates.

Sides, back and top can be framed with conventional lumber up to the steel studs and standoffs. No combustible material, electrical wiring, insulation, plastic vapor barrier or gas plumbing inside the steel stud framing; a full header above the kit is highly recommended. The lintel is fixed: the fireplace itself is positioned so the lintel's front face sets the finished face, and the framing brackets give 1 7/8" of adjustment.
Board, facing & hearth

Sheet the front with non-combustible board 12" above and 5 9/16" beside the framing edge bars. Facing up to 1 7/8" finishes flush; masonry may recess the unit up to 4 1/2". Keep the door and screen free to open.

• Board: cement board, calcium silicate board or equivalent; standard drywall may be used beyond that zone. Fix it with drywall screws and pre-drill the holes so the board doesn't crack. Calcium silicate is 1/2" thick and is damaged if dropped or struck; don't use a cracked board.
  • If the board won't be covered with other non-combustible material such as tile, make the top sections a single sheet; taped and mudded joints may crack from the heat.
  • Painted wall above the unit: discard the supplied framing kit and use full sheets of calcium silicate board (or equivalent) on full-length metal studs.
  • Recess beyond 4 1/2": move the facing away from the unit face and window, top and sides, at a 1:1 ratio, up to a maximum 12" deep.
  • A hearth extension is optional; a non-combustible hearth no more than 1" above the fireplace bottom is suggested. A thicker hearth means raising the fireplace accordingly.
  • Exterior wall or chase: insulate the outer walls like other exterior walls, cover insulation and vapor barrier with a solid surface such as drywall, keep the fireplace off the insulation, don't insulate inside the framing kit, and seal the chase at the ceiling or between floors.
Finishing material must not stop the glass door from opening in the event of ignition of excess gas buildup.
Electrical, wall switch & vent mode

Connect 110 V. AC in the junction box behind the right-side firebox access panel. Run the 40 ft. communication cable to the wall switch (check continuity before walling in), load its 4 "AA" batteries and set the PV/NV switch.

1. With the fireplace in its location, remove the glass door frame and the access panel on the right side of the firebox.
  2. Connect the 110 V. AC supply to the wires in the junction box (Figure 29); they can be reached from inside or outside the box through either small access panel.
  3. Mount the wall switch and route the supplied control cable; connect one end to the wall switch and the other to the interface board. Check the continuity of each wire first.
  4. Home automation: two cables, the top one to the fireplace and the bottom one to the home automation system.
  5. Insert the 4 supplied "AA" batteries into the wall switch battery pack.
  6. Set the PV/NV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one (power off and backup batteries out when switching).
  7. Install the burner per its kit instructions if it isn't already in place; turn on the gas, check that all connections are tight and leak free, then turn on gas and electrical supplies.
Gas supply + leak test

3/8" N.P.T. valve inlet, through the top or left side of the control box. Sediment trap within 6 feet of the valve and a union or flare fitting (don't hard pipe); check every connection is tight and leak free.

• Gas line by a qualified service person to all building codes; use the correct line diameter for proper operation and pressure.
  • Sediment trap per the national fuel gas code, no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve (also a warranty condition).
  • Provide a union or flare fitting so the valve can be disconnected for repair or replacement.
  • Connect the supply to the valve, turn on the gas and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); close its manual shut-off valve at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).
Reinstall the access panel and its gasket after installation, conversion or servicing; without it the control system overheats and fails early.
Check gas pressures

Fireplace lit on its highest setting: supply NG 5.0–13.9" WC, LP 12.5–13.9" WC; manifold NG 1.6–3.5" WC, LP 6.4–10" WC. Turn the gas off before pulling a test-port plug; the test procedure is in the Burner Installation Manual.
Vent & terminate

Town & Country kits only; screw and tape every joint, keep 1 ¾" to combustibles and give horizontal runs ¼" rise per ft. Wall: 2 foot min. off the top and a 14½" opening; roof: firestops and 12" min. above the roof. 68 feet max total.

• Wall: frame a 14½" opening (round or square) centred at least 68½" above the floor, higher for longer horizontal runs. Trim the wall thimble/shield to the wall thickness including siding, flush with the outer wall; thimble and vent must not protrude beyond the siding. Engage both inner and outer pipes in the terminal, fix it to the outside wall (not recessed) and caulk it.
  • Roof: a 14 ½" opening at each floor, ceiling or roof (larger as the pitch increases, to keep a 1¾" air space); avoid cutting rafters. Push the ceiling firestop up from below; into an attic leave its shield full length (attic insulation shield SKU #22270029 may be required) and add a storm collar on top. Roof support bracket to the joists, flashing sealed to the roof, storm collar with a thick ring of mastic, terminal cap screwed on and caulked.
  • Join components tightly and secure them with sheet metal screws, then wrap every outer joint completely with the supplied high-temperature self-adhesive aluminum tape.
  • Fit the insulated collar shield (Pt# TC36.9709, included) around the vent pipe flush with the top of the unit; bend the tabs over 180°.
  • Keep rise and run inside the charts (Figures 42 and 43, pp. 24–25); offsets per Figure 58 (p. 33).
Set the vent restrictor

Read the restrictor position for your vent height and horizontal length from the chart (Figure 51); loosen the plate screws, move the plates, retighten. It ships open and must be fully open with a power vent.

The restrictor, on the underside of the firebox top, adjusts secondary air for flame appearance and performance. Chart positions come from lab tests; the ideal position may vary slightly with the installation.

The chart (Figure 51) is a diagram of vent height against horizontal length; its zones are marked fully open, 3" open, 2" open and 1" open NG / 3/4" open LP. Read your setting from the diagram.

  • Closed too much: flame excessively tall and lifting, lacks movement, soots.
  • Too open: flame height low, excessive movement.

To adjust: loosen the screws holding the restrictor plates, move the plates to the intended opening, retighten.

The vent restrictor must be fully open when using the power vent.
Firebox panels, burner & trim

A firebox panel set must be installed for safe operation, before the logs, with the gas connection made first. Fit rear, side and front panels (Arch: one-piece rear and brow piece), then the magnetic transition trim and barrier screen.

TC36

  1. Remove the side panel retainer (two screws, between the firebox lip and the heat shield) and install the lower rear panel.
  2. Make the gas connection before installing the remaining panels.
  3. Right side panel: bottom in first, then angle it up into position (push the firebox shield up if needed). Then the rear upper panel and the left side panel.
  4. Reinstall the side panel retainers; install the left and right front panels.

Two "V" brackets on the rear wall hold the lower rear panel against the side panels; adjust their angle by hand for a snug fit.

TC36 Arch

One-piece rear panel, no "V" brackets: remove the brow piece (five screws behind its front flange), install the rear panel, make the gas connection, fit the right then the left side panel, reinstall the brow, then the front panels.

Trim and screen (pp. 36–38)

Transition trim kit 80002252 (TC36D2) / 80002253 (TC36D2 ARCH): with the door in place, fit the side pieces (two smaller magnets each), then the top piece over them (three larger magnets); rest the meshed bottom piece on the floor in the gap between the outer door frame and the glass, and put the Town & Country badge on its right-hand side. Attach the magnetic safety barrier screen to the outer door frame.

Don't use the fireplace without panels. They're very fragile: unpack and inspect them, and install them before the logs. Fibre panels need to be trimmed to fit (supplier manufacturing tolerances); porcelain panels have their own instruction manual. See the burner instructions before proceeding.
Pair the wall switch & remote
Wall switch selector to Remote, hold Program up to 10 seconds until 5 beeps; the fireplace answers 3 + 3. Then press Program once and the remote's on/off within 60 sec.; 3 beeps confirm.

Bluetooth wall switch

  1. Set the wall switch selector to the "Remote" setting.
  2. Press and hold the Program button (straightened paper clip) for up to 10 seconds; release after the wall switch beeps 5 times. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then another 3: fireplace and wall switch are linked.
  3. Press and release Program once (3 beeps from the wall switch), then press and release on/off on the remote handset within 60 sec. Three beeps: the remote is paired to the wall switch.

Cross-communication with another nearby fireplace: repeat step 2 to switch automatically to another of three channels.

Basic wall switch

The remote pairs directly to the module: press Program once (3 beeps from the module), press on/off on the remote within 60 sec., and the module beeps 3 times.

The TC Fire app (Apple and Android) is linked with the PIN on the wall switch sticker; that procedure is in the owner's manual.

light.title: Turning the fireplace on and off
light.html:
Your fireplace has an ignition device that lights the pilot for you. Don't try to light the pilot by hand.

Turn it on

  1. First, smell all around the fireplace for gas, including down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles there.
  2. Press On/Off on the remote. The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time.
  3. When the burner is lit, set the flame you want with the remote.

If the burner doesn't light

  1. Switch the fireplace off.
  2. Wait at least 5 minutes for any gas inside to escape.
  3. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety. If you don't, try again.

If it won't light or stay lit after several tries, switch it off, turn off all electric power to the fireplace and call your service technician or gas supplier.

Very first lighting: allow time for air to clear out of the gas line.

Turn it off

Press On/Off. For service or a long shutdown, also turn off all electric power to the fireplace and remove the backup batteries.

remote.title: Using the Proflame 2 remote
remote.html:
The remote has an On/Off key, a Thermostat key, a Mode key and up and down arrows, plus a backlit screen. It runs on 3 AAA batteries. When you turn the fireplace on or off, change the flame or light, or switch pilot mode, a single beep from the fireplace confirms it got the command.

Flame height

There are six flame levels. With the fireplace on, each press of the down arrow lowers the flame one step, until the flame is off. Each press of the up arrow raises it. If the fireplace is on but the flame is off, the up arrow brings the flame back on high.

Light dimmer

Press Mode until the light bulb icon shows, then use the arrows to pick one of six light levels.

Pilot mode

With the fireplace off, press Mode until the CPI icon shows. The up arrow switches to CPI (continuous pilot ignition). The down arrow switches back to IPI (intermittent pilot ignition).

Key lock

Press Mode and the up arrow together to lock the keys. A lock icon appears. Press them together again to unlock.

Thermostat: the remote's thermostat function is switched off at the factory. It isn't permitted in the USA.

sounds.title: First fire: smells and sounds
sounds.html:
A few things are normal the first times you use your fireplace.

A slight odor for a couple of hours

The first time it's lit, the fireplace gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. That's the paints, sealants and lubricants from manufacturing curing. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air out the room, because the odor can bother some people.

Ticking and creaking

Steel fireplaces make some expansion and contraction noises as they start up and cool down. You'll hear similar noises from a furnace or an oven.

A short wait to light

The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you turn the fireplace on.

A gas smell is different. Don't light anything, don't touch electrical switches and don't use a phone in the building. Call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone, or the fire department if you can't reach them.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, using a fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Only when it's cool. Don't clean the glass while it's hot.
  • No abrasive cleaners on the glass or any other part of the fireplace.
  • The outside finish can be cleaned with mild soap and water.
Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. Keep the barrier screen that came with the fireplace in place.

If the glass is cracked or broken

Don't use the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't strike the glass. A licensed or qualified service person should replace it, with ceramic glass only. Your Town & Country dealer can supply it; say whether your fireplace has a regular or an arched door.

wall.title: Wall switch & TC Fire app
wall.html:
Your fireplace is linked to the wall switch, and the remote is linked to the wall switch. If you ever need to pair them again, do it in this order.

1. Wall switch to fireplace

  1. Set the wall switch selector to "Remote."
  2. With a straightened paper clip, press and hold the Program button for up to 10 seconds.
  3. Let go after the wall switch beeps 5 times. The fireplace beeps 3 times, then 3 more. They're paired.

2. Remote to wall switch

Press and release Program once (3 beeps). Within 60 seconds, press On/Off on the remote. Three beeps from the wall switch mean it's paired.

If another nearby fireplace comes on instead of yours, repeat step 1. It moves to another of three channels.

TC Fire app

Get the free TC Fire app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Open Add/Edit Fireplace, tap Add, and enter the PIN from the sticker on the wall switch plus a name. The app turns the flame and the light on and off and sets their levels.

Remote not working? The on/off switch on the wall switch turns the fireplace on and off without it.

power.title: Power & batteries
power.html:
Your fireplace runs on house power. A backup battery pack can keep its control module (the IFC) working when the power goes out.

Remote3 × AAA
Wall switch battery pack4 × AA

In a power outage

The backup batteries are used only when house power is interrupted or lost, and only if your fireplace doesn't use a power vent.

Low batteries

  • Remote: a low-battery icon appears on the screen before the batteries run out. Until you replace them, you can use the on/off switch on the wall switch.
  • Control module: if it answers a command with a double beep instead of a single beep, its batteries are low. After you replace them, it beeps once again.
Before you remove or put back batteries, the manual says to turn off the main gas supply to the fireplace.

For service or a long shutdown, turn off the electric power and remove the backup batteries.

bulb.title: Replacing the light bulb
bulb.html:
The fireplace light sits in the top of the firebox. The parts list gives the bulb as a halogen light bulb 20W, part 80002650.

First, turn off the gas and the electrical power and give the fireplace plenty of time to cool.

Take out the old bulb

  1. Remove the screw holding the light cover to the upper heat shield, then pull the light assembly down slightly.
  2. Slip a small flat screwdriver between the glass lens and the light box, and twist it carefully to pop the lens open.
  3. Pull the old bulb away from the plug end while wiggling it gently.

Put in the new one

  1. Hold the new bulb with a paper towel or cloth. Oils from your skin can make it fail early. If you touch it by accident, clean it with alcohol before use.
  2. Push it into the plug end while wiggling it gently.
  3. Push the lens up to close it, fit the light assembly back into the light box and put the screw back in.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Call your gas supplier right away from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it. The barrier screen supplied with the fireplace must stay installed.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. If anyone at risk lives with you, an adjustable safety gate keeps them out of the room and away from hot surfaces.
  • Keep clothing, furniture, draperies, gasoline and other flammable liquids and vapors away from it.
  • Put back any panel or door removed for service before you use the fireplace.
  • Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
Been under water? Don't use the fireplace if any part has been under water. Call a qualified service technician immediately to inspect it and replace any part of the control system and any gas control that was under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the fireplace and its venting at least once a year. More frequent cleaning may be needed if there's a lot of lint from carpets or bedding.

What the yearly check covers

  • Removing the glass and checking the decorative media (logs, pebbles, glass) for soot. Heavy soot means the fireplace should be inspected and adjusted so it burns properly.
  • Cleaning the media, and cleaning the burner with a brush or vacuum, especially the burner ports.
  • Checking the pilot flame size and operation, and cleaning the pilot.
  • Making sure the vent pipe and the outside vent terminal are open and free of blockage or debris.
  • Checking the glass gasket. The glass seal must stay in good condition.
  • Checking and replacing batteries as needed.

Between visits, keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline and other flammable liquids and vapors.

Found a problem? Contact your dealer to have it repaired. Don't try to repair the fireplace yourself.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Town & Country's limited lifetime warranty for gas products covers the original registered purchaser.

Glass (thermal breakage only), combustion chamber, burner tube assembly, porcelain finishesLimited lifetime · parts only
Any part found defective2 years from purchase · parts and labor

Conditions

  • Installed by a qualified technician, following local and national requirements and the appliance manual.
  • A sediment trap within 6 feet of the gas control valve.
  • The installer makes sure it fires as per the rating plate.
  • Porcelain is warranted for gloss retention. Some colors darken when hot and return to their shade when cool.

Not covered

  • Parts showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident or lack of maintenance.
  • Mantels, surrounds or finishing material around the fireplace.
  • Installation, operating or environmental conditions beyond Town & Country's control.
Installing or operating it differently from the manual's instructions voids the warranty. This is a summary; the full terms are in the owner's manual.

From the rating label, on a plate in the slot between the left-hand lintel and the left-hand door frame (attached to the lintel with a cable). Listed to ANSI Z21.50-2019 / CSA 2.22-2019 Vented Gas Fireplaces and CAN/CGA 2.17-M91 (high altitudes).

  • Decorative product, not intended to be used as a heating appliance; not for use with solid fuel.
  • Only for the gas type on the rating plate; not convertible unless a certified kit is used.
  • For use only with the glass and screen barrier certified with the appliance.
  • Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room, and for an aftermarket, permanently located manufactured (mobile) home where not prohibited by local codes.

specInlet.title: Supply (inlet) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0" WC min · 13.9" WC max
Propane12.5" WC min · 13.9" WC max

The minimum is for the purpose of input adjustment. Verify with the fireplace lit and on its highest setting; turn off the gas supply before removing the plug from the supply pressure test port. The testing procedure is in the Burner Installation Manual. The rating label (p. 46) gives the same values: 5.0 / 12.5 in/wc minimum, 13.9 in/wc maximum.

  • Valve inlet: 3/8" N.P.T.; supply-line access holes at the top and left sides of the control box.
  • Sediment trap no more than 6 feet from the gas control valve; a union or flare fitting, never hard piped to the valve.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests: disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve above 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa); isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve at or below 1/2 psig (3.5 kPa).

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.6" WC min · 3.5" WC max
Propane6.4" WC min · 10" WC max

Measure at the manifold pressure test port (Figure 38) with the fireplace lit on its highest setting; turn the gas off before removing the port plug. The rating label lists the maximums as 3.5 in/wc (NG) and 10.0 in/wc (LP). Flame appearance is tuned with the vent restrictor (p. 30).

specTerm.title: Vent terminal clearances
specTerm.html:
Measure to the nearest edge of the termination hood. The vent terminal must not be recessed. Local codes or regulations may require different clearances; for USA installations follow the current National Fuel Gas Code, ANSI Z223.1.

A · Above grade, veranda, porch, deck or balcony12" (30 cm) min.
B · Window or door that may be opened12" (30 cm) min.
C · Permanently closed window (recommended, against condensation)12" (30 cm) min.
D · Ventilated soffit above, within 2 feet (60 cm) horizontally30" (76 cm) min.
E · Unventilated soffit30" (76 cm) min.
F · Outside corner6" (15 cm) min.
G · Inside corner6" (15 cm) min.
H · Above a meter/regulator assembly, horizontally from the regulator center-line3 feet (90 cm) min.
I · Service regulator vent outlet6 feet (1.8 m) min.
J · Non-mechanical air supply inlet, or another appliance's combustion air inlet12" (30 cm) min.
K · Mechanical air supply inlet6 feet (1.8 m) min.
L · Above a paved sidewalk or paved driveway on public property7 feet (2.1 m) min.
M · Under veranda, porch, deck or balcony30" (76 cm) min.

L: never directly above a sidewalk or paved driveway that lies between two single family dwellings and serves both. M: only if the veranda, porch, deck or balcony is fully open on a minimum of 2 sides beneath the floor. Starred values in the manual are as specified in the CGA B149 installation codes. Roof-terminal clearances to adjacent structures are shown only as a diagram (Figure 47).

Mantel to appliance (rating label)9 in. (229 mm)
Maximum mantel extension (rating label)12 in. (305 mm)

Mantel clearance and mantel depth step together on a lettered chart (Figure 3); read the steps from that diagram. Keep combustible material, electrical wiring and gas plumbing out of the non-combustible zone it marks. The unit may be recessed up to 4 1/2" with non-combustible masonry type material. Never connect it to a chimney flue serving a separate solid fuel burning appliance.

specElec.title: Electrical & controls
specElec.html:
Fireplace110 volts, 60Hz, 0.25A
Optional power vent kit115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A
Supply110 V. AC to the junction box
Wall switch cable40 ft. communication cable (supplied)
Wall switch batteries4 "AA" (supplied)
Note: p. 16 rates the optional power vent kit at 115 volts, 60Hz, 1.8A; the rating label on p. 46 lists a blower electrical rating of 115v, 60hz, 1.1 A next to the optional power vent kits.
  • Gas control system, junction box and interface board: right side of the firebox, behind the access panel (and the decorative firebox panel, if installed).
  • Check the continuity of each wire in the communication cable before plugging it into the wall switch and the IFC module, and before it is walled in.
  • PV/NV switch on the interface board: NV without a power vent, PV with one. When switching, turn off the electrical supply and remove the backup batteries to re-set the module. The vent restrictor must be fully open with a power vent.
  • Home automation, Bluetooth wall switch: dry-contact relay for flame and light on/off; 0 - 10 volt DC analog input for levels (Low = 1 volt, High = 10 volts); the control repeats a signal every 2 hours or until a new command. Basic wall switch: flame on/off only (solid brown wire and common). Wire not supplied.

specFacing.title: Framing, facing & hearth
specFacing.html:
Facing material, flush installup to 1 7/8" thick
Framing bracket adjustment1 7/8"
Recess with non-combustible masonryup to 4 1/2"
Deeper recessfacing moved back 1:1, top and sides, to a maximum 12" deep
Non-combustible backing board12" above · 5 9/16" to the sides of the framing edge bars
Calcium silicate board1/2" thick
Hearth (optional, non-combustible)no more than 1" above the fireplace bottom

A 3/4" facing thickness lets the finish sit flush with the front of the unit (p. 9). The lintel is fixed, so its front face sets the fireplace's final position; allow for the facing thickness before settling it. Facing must not stop the door or the screen from opening. A hearth extension isn't required and combustible flooring may run up to the fireplace, but materials such as wood flooring may discolor, shrink and crack from the radiant heat. With a hearth thicker than 1" the fireplace must be raised accordingly; thicker hearth extensions interfere with opening the safety screen and door frame. Minimum combustible framing dimensions are diagrams (Figures 11 and 12, p. 10).

review.notes: Both manuals cover the TC36D2 and TC36D2 ARCH (rating label: TC36 / TC36AR, Series D); the guide covers both and calls out Arch differences (framing kit, panels, trim, glass). The rating label (doc 1 p. 46) is the only source for input rates, efficiency, listing and altitude; the owner's manual has no specs. Catalog max BTU (47,000 NG/LP), efficiency (26.8%, P.4.1-15, given once, not split by fuel) and ignition (IPI/CPI selectable, doc 2 pp. 7, 10) match; catalog view area (983 sq in) is not in either manual. Catalog features not stated in these manuals: 'up to 110 ft' power venting (manual only says power vents need different venting, see power vent manuals) and 'switched to standing pilot' (manual: CPI, continuous pilot ignition). Listing is ANSI Z21.50-2019 / CSA 2.22-2019 (decorative vented gas fireplace, not a heater) plus CAN/CGA 2.17-M91, not Z21.88. Burner, media, fuel conversion and the gas pressure test procedure are in a separate Burner Installation Manual (referenced doc 1 pp. 16, 20, 34) that isn't one of this guide's sources, so there is no fuel conversion card. Shown only as diagrams, so not transcribed: fireplace dimensions (Figs 1-2, p. 5), mantel clearance/depth chart A-F (Fig. 3, p. 6; guide uses the rating label's 9 in. / 12 in.), framing kit and minimum combustible framing dimensions (Figs 10-12, pp. 9-10), roof opening A/B by pitch (Fig. 44, p. 26), roof clearance to adjacent structures (Fig. 47, p. 28), vent restrictor zones (Fig. 51, p. 30), vent offsets (Fig. 58, p. 33), wiring (p. 45). The wall and roof rise/run tables (pp. 24-25) are clean in the raw text but only their limits are used. Batteries: doc 1 p. 16 puts 4 AA in the wall switch battery pack; doc 2 p. 7 describes an IFC backup battery pack without size or location; the guide lists both without equating them. Thermostat is disabled by default and not permissible in the USA (doc 2 p. 6), so the Canadian enable procedure (p. 9) is left out. Facing: p. 9 says a 3/4" thickness finishes flush, p. 15 says flush installs take facing up to 1 7/8" (framing bracket range 1 7/8", p. 14); read as compatible, both shown in the specFacing drawer. Doc 2 p. 7 mentions Proflame 2 comfort fan control generically; no fan is documented for the TC36, so no blower tile. 'Turn off main gas supply ... prior to removing or reinserting the batteries' (doc 2 p. 6) is passed on as printed. Minor errata not flagged: roof support bracket 80001286 (p. 26) vs 800001286 (p. 31), part not used in the guide; p. 17 says pairing is on pages 38/39 (actually pp. 39-40); owner's TOC lists the warranty on p. 21 (it is p. 20); p. 34 'fibre panels made need to be trimmed' quoted as 'need to be trimmed'. Doc 1 p. 47 and doc 2 pp. 21-23 have no text. No code table in either manual, so codes are empty; beep signals are described in the owner drawers.
